disease.inheritance: Autosomal dominant, de novo (sporadic) — heterozygous LMNA c.1824C>T (p.Gly608Gly) cryptic splice-site variant
disease.mechanism: Gain-of-function / toxic protein. The c.1824C>T (p.Gly608Gly) variant activates a cryptic splice donor in LMNA exon 11, causing an in-frame deletion of 50 codons of prelamin A. The resulting isoform 'progerin' retains its C-terminal CAAX box and is farnesylated, but lacks the ZMPSTE24 cleavage site (which lies within the deleted region), so it remains permanently farnesylated and anchors at the nuclear lamina, disrupting nuclear architecture.
disease.autotac_rationale: Progerin is a toxic gain-of-function protein; selective degradation is mechanistically appropriate (in principle). NOTE: the approved drug lonafarnib is NOT an AUTOTAC — see treatment.
disease.prevalence: ~1 in 4 million (commonly cited; some sources state 1 in 8 million) — UNVERIFIED exact figure this session, requires confirmation against GeneReviews/Orphanet

approved_treatments.mechanism_correct: Inhibits farnesyltransferase, blocking the farnesylation step required for progerin to anchor at the nuclear envelope — thereby reducing toxic progerin accumulation. It does NOT bind LMNA/progerin directly.
approved_treatments.note: First and only FDA-approved therapy for HGPS. Slows disease progression; not curative.

disease.combination_therapy: Lonafarnib + pravastatin + zoledronic acid (farnesylation inhibitor triple, Circulation 2016, PMID 27400896)
investigational: CRISPR base editing to correct the c.1824C>T splice variant (preclinical)
Progerin-targeting PROTAC/AUTOTAC degraders (investigational, not yet clinical)

disease.human_summary: Children with HGPS age ~8x faster than normal. Growth failure, hair loss, skin changes, and premature atherosclerosis lead to death from heart attack or stroke at a median age of ~14.5 years.
disease.clinical_trials_note: 5 curated interventional trials; 11 ClinicalTrials.gov studies in total (2026-11-07)
